context:
Add re-exports, update imports, add a test. No new packages, no
compatibility shims, no distribution split.
description:
BenchBox's MCP server consumes 23+ core APIs. Most are already public, but
3 are internal module references that MCP imports directly:

| Symbol                      | Current location                        |
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| TPCH_DATAFRAME_QUERIES      | benchbox.core.tpch.dataframe_queries    |
| TPCDS_DATAFRAME_QUERIES     | benchbox.core.tpcds.dataframe_queries   |
| DATAFRAME_PLATFORMS          | benchbox.platforms.dataframe             |

These should be promoted to public exports (re-exported from a stable
location like `benchbox.api` or `benchbox.__init__`) so MCP is not coupled
to internal module paths.

MCP is already gated behind an optional extra (`benchbox[mcp]`) and the
dependency direction is already one-way (MCP depends on core, core never
imports MCP). No distribution split is needed at this time.

anti_patterns.dont: add backwards-compatibility shims for the old internal import paths
change MCP schemas or prompt contracts as part of this work
split MCP into a separate distribution at this stage

preserves.behavior: MCP server behavior and schema semantics unchanged
benchbox[mcp] optional extra install path unchanged

verifications.description: MCP tests still pass with updated imports
Public exports test confirms the 3 symbols are accessible
Core CLI and documentation tests unaffected
